name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia and Myelodysplastic Syndromes Related to Alkylating Agent

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: History of prior exposure to alkylating agents or radiation therapy
Presence of persistent cytopenias (anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia)
Morphological evidence of dysplasia in one or more myeloid cell lines
Detection of clonal cytogenetic abnormalities typical of alkylating agent-related disease (e.g., monosomy 5 or 7)
Bone marrow blast percentage ≥20% for AML or 5-19% for MDS

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: History of alkylating agent exposure plus cytopenias and dysplastic hematopoiesis with blast count criteria met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of de novo AML/MDS and consideration of latency period (typically 2-7 years post-exposure).

pathognomonic.notes: Reduction in all blood cell lines

searchTerms: bone marrow not making enough cells
marrow failure causing low blood counts

common.notes: Increased susceptibility to bacterial and fungal infections
searchTerms: recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.symptomName: Petechiae and mucosal bleeding due to thrombocytopenia
common.notes: Bleeding manifestations secondary to low platelet count
searchTerms: petechiae and bleeding from low platelets
mucosal bleeding and small red spots

common.notes: Symptoms related to decreased oxygen carrying capacity

searchTerms: tiredness due to low blood count

occasional.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to extramedullary hematopoiesis
Due to marrow expansion or leukemic infiltration
Often related to infection or disease activity

rare.notes: Rare but severe complication due to high blast count
searchTerms: lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing blasts and dysplastic cells
Bone marrow biopsy with increased blasts and dysplasia
imaging: Chest X-ray may show infiltrates in leukostasis
genetic: Clonal chromosomal abnormalities typical of alkylating agent-related AML/MDS
Mutations in TP53, RUNX1, or ASXL1 genes
other: History of prior chemotherapy or radiation exposure
Latency period of 2-7 years post alkylating agent exposure

distinguishingFeatures: No prior exposure to alkylating agents

redFlags: High blast count in peripheral blood or bone marrow
Signs of leukostasis such as respiratory distress or neurological deficits
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Vardiman JW, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2016.
